'''''Gomphrena pulchella''''', the '''pink globe amaranth''', is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Amaranthaceae|amaranth]] family native to [[Paraguay]], Northern [[Argentina]], and many of the surrounding areas, as well as parts of northeastern [[Brazil]] where it grows primarily in [[Cerrado|cerrado grasslands]]. It's also been introduced to southeastern [[Mexico]] and can be seen in gardens outside of that [[Range (biology)|range]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Gillette |first=Barbara |date=September 3, 2024 |title=How to Grow and Care for Gomphrena |url=https://www.thespruce.com/gomphrena-care-guide-7555301 |access-date=August 13, 2026 |website=The Spruce}}</ref><ref name=POWO>{{Cite POWO |title=''Gomphrena pulchella'' Mart. |id=60569-1 |access-date=19 July 2026}}</ref>

== Description ==
''Gomphrena pulchella'' has long, straight stems of about {{cvt|30-50|cm|in}} tall with a woody base and short hairs on most of it. The leaves are lance-like, and occur directly across from each other on the stem. The [[inflorescence]]s are purplish pink and are in dense round clusters at the top of the stem. The true flowers are small and yellow, and mostly inconspicuous.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ochoa |last2=Catan |last3=Targa |last4=Fraño |last5=Caro |last6=Chaila |date=2022 |title=Morphoanatomic characterization of Gomphrena perennis and Gomphrena pulchella leaves 
|url=https://www.scielo.br/j/aws/a/LdpPwG5gZ7jLDNLnLCrhMPS/?format=pdf&lang=en |journal=Advances in Weed Science |pages=1|first1=Maria del C |first2=Alejandra |first3=Maria G |first4=Alicia |first5=Roque |first6=Salvador}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Balogh |first=Anne |date=August 3, 2022 |title=Grow Gomphrena Flowers for Long-Lasting Color |url=https://www.gardendesign.com/annuals/gomphrena.html |access-date=July 19, 2026 |website=Garden Design}}</ref>

== Nomenclature ==
''Gomphrena pulchella'' is known by a variety of [[Common name|common names]]. Often, it is generalized as a globe amaranth as a member of the genus [[Gomphrena]], a name it shares with ''[[Gomphrena globosa|G. globosa]]''. When referring to the specific species, it takes the common name of pink globe amaranth, or the Truffula pink globe amaranth, or simply Truffula pink, the latter two of which are specific to commercial applications; such as selling or advertising.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Truffula Pink - Globe Amaranth - Gomphrena |url=https://www.provenwinners.com/plants/gomphrena/truffula-pink-globe-amaranth-gomphrena-pulchella |access-date=2026-08-13 |website=Proven Winners |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Truffula Pink Globe Amaranth (Gomphrena pulchella) |url=https://www.plantstogrow.com/P/5456/TruffulaPinkGlobeAmaranthGomphrenapulchella |access-date=2026-08-13 |website=www.plantstogrow.com}}</ref>

Occasionally, ''G. Pulchella'' may be known as a fireworks cultivar or fireworks ''Gomphrena''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gomphrena pulchella, 'Fireworks' |url=https://www.chilternseeds.co.uk/item_646p_gomphrena_pulchella_fireworks_seeds?srsltid=AfmBOornNYg3xTanxERUuwc-8zT17who5dguQvZsdjpBK7v5ZTqBqt9z |access-date=August 13, 2026 |website=Chiltern Seeds}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Fireworks Gomphrena |url=https://plants.rogersgardens.com/12290002/Plant/17579/Fireworks_Gomphrena/ |access-date=August 13, 2026 |website=Roger's Gardens}}</ref>
